content: {"findings": [{"file": "src/review_agents/mirror.py", "line_start": 106, "line_end": 111, "severity": "blocking", "title": "Refspec is built from the URL after `--`, but refs are concatenated without `--` protection or remote name", "why": "The fetch passes `url` followed by refspecs; git treats the first non-option as the remote and the rest as refspecs, which is fine. But the refspecs are formed from validated refs only; validation rejects spaces and ' :^~?*[\\' so injection is limited. However `ref` can contain `..` (e.g. `refs/heads/..foo`) which the regex allows, and more importantly a ref can be `refs/heads/x` with a leading `-`? Refs must start with `refs/` so no leading dash. This is probably not blocking."}, {"file": "src/review_agents/mirror.py", "line_start": 113, "line_end": 120, "severity": "blocking", "title": "Fetch into an existing mirror can race with readers using `cat-file` while the mirror is being written", "why": "`_locked` only serializes writers; `has_commit` and tool reads (`RepoTools` using `run_git` on the same git_dir) run without taking the lock. Git fetch updates refs and packs the object store concurrently with readers. `git fetch` writes new packfiles but normally is safe for readers, however a concurrent `git gc`/repack or pruning from fetch's auto-maintenance could delete loose objects a reader is about to open, and `cat-file` could see a partially written object. More importantly `RepoTools` is constructed with the git_dir and reads it long after sync returns, but if another sync runs concurrently for the same repo (another review), the ref updates under `refs/heads/main` don't affect `cat-file <sha>:path` since the sha is fixed, so object reads are safe as long as objects aren't pruned. Auto-gc from fetch (`gc.auto`) can prune unreachable objects while a reader holds only the sha, causing "object not found" errors mid-review. This is a real robustness/racing issue: the reviewer should disable auto-gc or take a shared lock during reads."}, {"file": "src/review_agents/tools.py", "line_start": 95, "line_end": 100, "severity": "important", "title": "`git grep` uses `-E` with agent-controlled regex, and invalid regex raises GitError but very expensive regex (ReDoS) can hang the review", "why": "The pattern is passed to `git grep -E` with no complexity limit; a pathological regex like `(a+)+$` over a large blob will backtrack and consume CPU indefinitely (git's regex engine is largely regexec/PCRE depending on build, but still catastrophic for POSIX ERE in some cases). There's no timeout on `subprocess.run`, so a malicious or careless agent can wedge the review worker. Also `search_code` runs `git grep` over the whole commit with no path restriction, so a large repository search can be expensive; combined with no timeout this is a liveness problem."}, {"file": "src/review_agents/tools.py", "line_start": 108, "line_end": 118, "severity": "important", "title": "Skip-list filtering parses `path` by splitting on the first ':' — paths containing ':' are mis-detected", "why": "`location.split(\":\", 1)[0]` assumes output lines are `path:line: text`. Git's `--no-line-number`-style formatting is enabled with `-n`, but git grep prefixes the commit as `<sha>:<path>:<line>:<text>`. After `removeprefix(f\"{commit}:\")`, a repository path containing a colon (allowed on POSIX) will be truncated at the first colon, so `is_skipped(path)` checks the wrong path. A skipped file like `fixtures/a:b.txt` would be reported as `fixtures/a` which may not match `fixtures/**`, leaking skipped content. Also `path_glob` filtering uses the truncated path, giving wrong results."}, {"file": "src/review_agents/tools.py", "line_start": 158, "line_end": 175, "severity": "important", "title": "`read_issue` follows HTTP redirects to arbitrary hosts with the Authorization header", "why": "`urllib.request.urlopen` follows redirects by default. The initial URL is fixed to `_api_base`, but a 30x response from GitHub (or a compromised/MITM'd endpoint, or a non-default `api_base` in tests) can redirect to `http://attacker/...`, and urllib will forward the `Authorization: Bearer <token>` header to the new location (urllib copies headers on redirect, and the token is attached unconditionally). This leaks the read-only GitHub token. Should disable redirects or strip the Authorization header on cross-origin redirect."}, {"file": "src/review_agents/tools.py", "line_start": 158, "line_end": 175, "severity": "robustness", "title": "`read_issue` does not bound response size; a huge issue body/labels can exhaust memory", "why": "`urlopen().read()` loads the entire response into memory via `json.load(response)`. The body is truncated to `MAX_ISSUE_CHARS` only after parsing, and `labels` are not bounded. A very large (or maliciously crafted, e.g. via a repo the reviewer controls) issue can consume unbounded memory. Redirect/Content-Length limits should be enforced."}, {"file": "src/review_agents/tools.py", "line_start": 175, "line_end": 178, "severity": "important", "title": "`labels = \", \".join(...)` crashes on non-dict/missing keys and body/title are accessed with `[]` — KeyError/TypeError becomes unhandled, surfacing as a 500 instead of a ToolError", "why": "`issue['title']` and `issue['state']` are accessed directly; if GitHub returns an unexpected payload (or a partial response for a different API shape), a `KeyError` propagates out of `read_issue`. That is not caught by `ToolBudget` (which only catches `ToolError`), so the whole agent call fails. Same for `label['name']` if a label is malformed."}, {"file": "src/review_agents/tools.py", "line_start": 95, "line_end": 99, "severity": "important", "title": "`git grep` can be made to read skippable/binary content into the match buffer and the result is not bounded in size before filtering", "why": "`git grep` is invoked with `--` nowhere; the `pattern` and `commit` come before the pattern. With `-e pattern`, the pattern is safe from being interpreted as an option. However there's no path restriction passed to git grep, so every blob at the commit is scanned, including huge files that would otherwise be rejected by `MAX_FILE_BYTES`. `-I` skips binary but not size. A large tracked text file (or many matches) will be materialized fully from git grep's stdout before the Python-side match cap of 100 applies. This is a memory/CPU amplification on untrusted repo content."}, {"file": "src/review_agents/tools.py", "line_start": 125, "line_end": 126, "severity": "important", "title": "`list_dir` splits `ls-tree -l` output on whitespace, breaking for names with spaces or special characters", "why": "`meta.split()` splits the metadata columns by whitespace, which works, but `line.split(\"\\t\", 1)` is fine. The real issue: `ls-tree` quotes paths with special characters by default (core.quotePath), so names with non-ASCII or control chars are shown escaped, and a path containing a tab or newline would break `line.split(\"\\t\", 1)` or produce wrong names. Should pass `-z` and parse NUL-separated entries. A crafted filename with a tab/newline in the PR can corrupt or spoof directory listings."}, {"file": "src/review_agents/tools.py", "line_start": 155, "line_end": 160, "severity": "robustness", "title": "`git_log` does not pass `--` before `self._commit` and appends path after `--`; but `_clean_path` allows an empty string and a path that begins with `-` isn't possible after `--`. However `path` with leading dashes reaches git after `--`, safe. Bug: log is not restricted to first-parent or ordered, but the bigger issue is `_git` raises `GitError` (not `ToolError`), so a bad sha/path failure leaks as uncaught", "why": "`self._git(*args)` will raise `GitError` on failure. `git_log` doesn't catch it, so a `GitError` (e.g. from a corrupted mirror or an invalid commit) escapes `ToolBudget.wrap` (which only catches `ToolError`), breaking the tool contract that tool errors are returned as text to the agent rather than crashing the call. Same for `read_file`'s second `cat-file blob` call (only the `-t`/`-s` calls are wrapped) and `list_dir`'s `split` of malformed lines."}, {"file": "src/review_agents/tools.py", "line_start": 82, "line_end": 89, "severity": "important", "title": "`read_file` `cat-file blob` can return an object larger than the `-s` size check due to TOCTOU / different object, and decoding unbounded data", "why": "The size check reads the size and then a second `cat-file blob` reads the content by the same ref path; if the commit is fixed this is stable, so no true TOCTOU. Not a real finding — omit."}, {"file": "src/review_agents/mirror.py", "line_start": 96, "line_end": 100, "severity": "important", "title": "`git_env` builds the config key from `remote_prefix` but `remote_prefix` is caller-controlled and not validated; a malformed prefix yields a config key that git rejects, failing all fetches", "why": "`http.{remote_prefix}.extraheader` — if `remote_prefix` contains characters git's config parser dislikes (e.g. newline) or is empty, the key is invalid and git errors out. More critically, in `MirrorStore.sync`, `remote_prefix=self._remote_base` which can be any URL (including one with a port, e.g. `http://127.0.0.1:1234`), and git config keys with `:` are allowed, so this works. Not blocking."}, {"file": "src/review_agents/mirror.py", "line_start": 76, "line_end": 80, "severity": "blocking", "title": "Secret masking only replaces the raw token, but git errors may contain the base64 header or credentials — and the token is passed to `fetch` but `secret` masking doesn't cover the base64 form", "why": "If git prints the extraheader value (it normally doesn't, but `-v` or certain errors can echo config), the base64-encoded credential `x-access-token:<token>` would appear, and `message.replace(secret, '***')` only masks the plain token, not the base64 form. Also the token character set: if the token itself appears base64-split across lines... marginal. More importantly, the check `if secret:` uses the raw token; the base64 header contains `x-access-token:{token}` so masking the raw token does catch the inner token text, but the surrounding base64 is still partially present. This is a minor leak but not full."}, {"file": "src/review_agents/mirror.py", "line_start": 113, "line_end": 122, "severity": "important", "title": "`init --bare` on an empty/missing git_dir, but `git_dir.parent.mkdir` is done in `_locked` only for `git_dir.parent`; the lock file is created in `git_dir.parent` with mode from `umask`, and the mirror directory itself has no explicit permission restriction — token isn't written but the mirror may be world-readable", "why": "`/data/repos/<owner>/<name>.git` is created with default umask under a directory owned by the `review` user. If the volume is shared or the container runs with a permissive umask, the mirror contents (potentially private repository code) are readable by other users/processes. There's no `os.umask` or `mkdir(mode=0o700)` on the repo dirs. For a private-repo mirror this is a data exposure."}, {"file": "src/review_agents/mirror.py", "line_start": 100, "line_end": 105, "severity": "robustness", "title": "`subprocess.run` has no timeout; a hung git fetch (network stall, auth prompt despite GIT_TERMINAL_PROMPT=0, server that trickles) blocks the lock forever, wedging all reviews of that repo", "why": "`run_git` runs git with no timeout. Under the exclusive flock, a hung `git fetch` holds the lock indefinitely; every other review of that repository then blocks on `flock(lock, LOCK_EX)` with no timeout. A slow or malicious remote (or a partial network partition) can deadlock the review queue. Add a timeout and/or lock timeout."}, {"file": "src/review_agents/mirror.py", "line_start": 127, "line_end": 135, "severity": "important", "title": "Missing-commit check happens inside the lock but `has_commit` is a static method called with git_dir; if fetch succeeds but the requested commit is only reachable via a shallow/pruned ref, this errors — fine. The real issue: a commit in `commits` that is an ancestor not on the fetched refs won't be present, raising MissingCommitError even though it exists upstream", "why": "`sync` fetches only the given `refs`. If `commits` includes a sha that is reachable from the PR head ref, it will be present. But if the caller passes a merge-base or base sha that is not an ancestor of the fetched refs in the local mirror (e.g. the default branch wasn't among `refs` and the base commit is only on a different branch), `has_commit` returns False and sync raises. The contract says 'Every commit must be present afterwards' but the implementation only fetches `refs`, not the commits themselves. If a caller relies on syncing arbitrary commits, it breaks. Either fetch the shas directly or document/enforce the dependency."}, {"file": "src/review_agents/tools.py", "line_start": 36, "line_end": 52, "severity": "blocking", "title": "`_glob_regex` is `@cache`d on attacker-influenced `pattern`, and `glob_match` compiles regex from skip-list patterns and `path_glob` — catastrophic regex construction / unbounded cache", "why": "`_glob_regex` is `functools.cache`d with no eviction. The `pattern` for skip paths comes from `skip_paths` (repo config, bounded), but `path_glob` comes directly from the agent. An agent can call `search_code(pattern, path_glob=...)` with many distinct glob strings, growing the cache unbounded (memory leak per process, since `cache` never evicts). Also `re.compile` on the translated pattern is fast, but `glob_match` uses `fullmatch`; a pathological glob like `**/**/**/...` translates to nested `.*` which can cause catastrophic backtracking on long paths (ReDoS) during `list_dir`/`search_code`, hanging the agent. There is no length limit on patterns or watch on the cache."}, {"file": "src/review_agents/tools.py", "line_start": 190, "line_end": 196, "severity": "important", "title": "`glob_match` compiles raw `**` into `.*` nested under `(?:.*/)?`, and `fullmatch` with uncontrolled patterns enables ReDoS on reviewer paths", "why": "Glob `src/**/x/**/y/**/z` with many `**` segments on a long path causes exponential backtracking. Since `path_glob` is agent-supplied and applied per file in a repo, a malicious/naive glob can pin CPU. Also skip_paths from repo config are trusted-ish, but an agent could pass such a glob as `path_glob`. Bound the pattern length and/or use a non-backtracking matcher."}, {"file": "src/review_agents/tools.py", "line_start": 184, "line_end": 190, "severity": "robustness", "title": "`ToolBudget.wrap` increments `used` before the call and catches only `ToolError`; other exceptions (GitError, KeyError, UnicodeDecodeError, socket errors from `read_issue`) propagate and abort the agent instead of being returned as text", "why": "The design promises tools return errors as text, but only `ToolError` is caught. `GitError` from `_git` in `read_file` (second cat-file), `list_dir` (only first call wrapped), and `git_log`; `KeyError`/`TypeError` from `read_issue`; `ValueError` from int parsing size; `UnicodeDecodeError` are not converted. Any of these crashes the tool call, which for a LangChain agent may terminate the agent mid-review. Should catch `GitError` (and be defensive around external JSON) and convert to `ToolError`/error text."}, {"file": "src/review_agents/tools.py", "line_start": 141, "line_end": 147, "severity": "robustness", "title": "`list_dir` line parsing crashes on `ls-tree` quoted/special names; `_` unpacking of `meta.split()` with 5 fields assumes format", "why": "`meta, name = line.split(\"\\t\", 1)` then `_, kind, _, size = meta.split()` expects exactly 4 whitespace-separated fields (`mode type sha size`). For submodule entries (`commit` kind) and for trees, size is `-`. That's fine. But if a name contains a newline, `ls-tree` output splits it into multiple lines and `line.split(\"\\t\", 1)` raises ValueError (uncaught). A PR that adds a file with a newline in the name (or non-ASCII triggering quotePath) can break or spoof listings. Should use `-z` and handle quoting."}, {"file": "src/review_agents/tools.py", "line_start": 108, "line_end": 118, "severity": "robustness", "title": "`git grep` output parsing assumes `path:line:text` and strips only `commit:` prefix; a path containing a newline or a match line containing `:` is mis-parsed, and the first-colon split is wrong for paths with colons", "why": "Same as earlier colon-in-path issue: `location.split(\":\", 1)[0]` yields the wrong path for any file whose name contains `:`, letting a skipped file bypass the skip filter and be returned to the agent (content leak of skipped files) or be wrongly excluded."}, {"file": "tests/test_tools.py", "line_start": 59, "line_end": 66, "severity": "robustness", "title": "Test creates a symlink in the work tree but the fixture's second commit only stages files; the symlink test passes only because the first commit's symlink was committed by `git add -A` — order-dependent and brittle", "why": "In the fixture, `os.symlink(...)` is created after the first `upstream.commit(...)` (which already ran `git add -A`), then a second `upstream.commit(...)` with other files runs `git add -A`, picking up the symlink. This works but is confusing; not a product bug. Not reporting."}, {"file": "src/review_agents/mirror.py", "line_start": 119, "line_end": 121, "severity": "blocking", "title": "`fetch` uses the URL as the remote without `--no-write-fetch-head` and without restricting which config the remote can set; a malicious repo cannot set config but `url.*.insteadOf`/`http.*` from env is fine. The real bug: `run_git(git_dir, \"fetch\", ...)` passes `--git-dir` but the command also needs to not read the repo's own config? It does read `git_dir/config`, which is attacker-influenced only by whoever writes the mirror. Fine. However: no `--no-recurse-submodules`, so if a fetched commit's tree has `.gitmodules` and the caller ever fetches with `--recurse-submodules` it would run hooks. Not triggered here."}, {"file": "src/review_agents/mirror.py", "line_start": 119, "line_end": 120, "why": "Fetch does not pass `--no-tags` is present, good. But there is no protection against the remote rewriting existing refs pointing at objects that would be needed: refspec uses `+`, forced update, which is fine for a mirror."}, {"file": "src/review_agents/tools.py", "line_start": 50, "line_end": 53, "severity": "important", "title": "`@cache` on `_glob_regex` is module-global and never cleared; agent-supplied `path_glob` values accumulate forever", "why": "A long-lived process running many reviews with agents supplying arbitrary `path_glob` strings will grow the cache unbounded (memory leak). Since `path_glob` is not part of `skip_paths` (trusted config), attacker/agent input pollutes a process-global cache. Use a bounded cache or `lru_cache(maxsize=...)`."}, {"file": "src/review_agents/tools.py", "line_start": 184, "line_end": 192, "severity": "robustness", "title": "`ToolBudget.wrap` increments `used` even when tool returns `LIMIT_REACHED`-past calls? No: past limit it returns early without incrementing. Fine. But it counts calls that error, which matches tests. No bug."}, {"file": "src/review_agents/mirror.py", "line_start": 66, "line_end": 71, "severity": "robustness", "title": "`run_git` sets `env=env or git_env()` but when a caller passes an env it completely replaces the base env, so `git_env()` defaults (no prompts, etc.) are lost unless the caller built via `git_env`", "why": "`env or git_env()`: an empty dict from a caller falls back, but a partially populated env would drop `GIT_TERMINAL_PROMPT=0` etc. All current callers use `git_env`, but the API invites passing a bare dict, which would re-enable prompts (hang) or read user config. Should merge rather than replace, or make `env` required to be a full env."}, {"file": "src/review_agents/tools.py", "line_start": 158, "line_end": 160, "severity": "robustness", "title": "`urllib.request.Request` with `Authorization` header but no `User-Agent` — GitHub API requires a User-Agent and returns 403 without it", "why": "GitHub's REST API rejects requests without a User-Agent header (HTTP 403). `read_issue` sets only Accept and optionally Authorization, so in production against `api.github.com` it will fail with 403 even with a valid token, returning a generic ToolError. Must set `User-Agent` (and ideally `X-GitHub-Api-Version`)."}, {"file": "src/review_agents/tools.py", "line_start": 155, "line_end": 178, "severity": "important", "title": "`read_issue` does not set a User-Agent, which GitHub requires; also `json.load` reads unbounded body", "why": "Combining: missing User-Agent causes GitHub to 403, and the response body is fully buffered. Set User-Agent and cap response size."}]}
